title: A Real Imitation

description.main: Tommy Kha's early book uses performance, self-portraiture and pictures of the Memphis landscape to work through growing up gay and of Chinese descent in his hometown. Introduction by Jon Feinstein. Published by Aint-Bad Editions, Savannah, in late 2015 as a perfect-bound paperback in a signed and numbered edition of 450.
description.extended:
An early book by the Memphis-born photographer Tommy Kha (b. 1988), A Real Imitation uses staged self-portraiture to work through growing up gay and of Chinese descent in the city he still calls home.

Across 80 pages the book mixes performance, self-portraits and pictures of Memphis landmarks and interiors. Kha appears as a deadpan figure beside a much larger white man, next to a cardboard cutout of Elvis, or in bed between two parental figures. These are sequenced with what he calls test shots: empty rooms and historic sites such as the Sun Studio interior that stand in for home. Jon Feinstein of Humble Arts Foundation contributes the introduction. Aint-Bad Editions of Savannah published it in late 2015 as a perfect-bound paperback in a signed and numbered edition of 450.

Kha took a BFA at Memphis College of Art and an MFA at Yale, where he now teaches. Self-portraiture, his family's passage from China through Vietnam to the American South, and the Memphis landscape run through his later work. Half, Full, Quarter (Aperture, 2023) came out of the Aperture–Baxter St Next Step Award, with an essay by Hua Hsu and a conversation with An-My Lê. Ghost Bites was shown at Baxter St at the Camera Club of New York. The 2025 Hayes Prize exhibition at the Addison Gallery of American Art was his first solo museum show.
description.artist_bio: Tommy Kha (b. Memphis, 1988) lives between Brooklyn and Memphis. BFA Memphis College of Art 2011, MFA Yale School of Art 2013; he now teaches at Yale. Aperture–Baxter St Next Step Award 2021, NYSCA/NYFA Artist Fellow 2022, Hayes Prize 2025 (Addison Gallery of American Art), Guggenheim Fellow 2025. Joined Higher Pictures in 2022. First major monograph Half, Full, Quarter (Aperture, 2023).

notes: publisher.url is the book's own product page on aint-bad.com (sold out). The publisher page gives size, pages, binding, edition, ISBN and the Feinstein introduction but no year. 2015 comes from Printed Matter, AbeBooks and Humble Arts ('published in late 2015'); the publisher's image uploads are dated 2015/12. Launch events ran into 2016. Printed Matter lists 25 x 20 cm, paperback, signed and numbered, edition 450. 'signed' is true because the whole edition is signed and numbered; confirm against the shelf copy. The kissing-strangers series and Elvis impersonation are not confirmed as part of this book in any saved source, so they were left out. Printed Matter does confirm a cardboard cutout of Elvis appears. Ghost Bites year is not on the Baxter St page. Getty SRU returned 0 records; Google Books 429; OpenLibrary 0. Existing cover kept: flat front cover, 884x1098. The publisher's own images are angled product shots on a map, not better.
